To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hygrothermal ageing effect can be significant and the hygroscopic swelling is significant comparing with thermal expansion of the underfill material.
the moisture diffusivity and the coefficient of hygrothermal expansion are strongly temperature dependent, and that the material exhibits non-Fickian behavior at higher humidity conditions.

the moisture diffusion behavior in the underfill can be well described with the Fickian model at low RH conditions, the hygroscopic swelling is significant and it increases with temperature, and hygrothermal aging induces damage in the underfills.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the moisture absorption and hygrothermal ageing of underfill materials, which are important factors that affect the reliability of flip-chip assemblies.
the characterization of the diffusion behavior, the swelling strain and the damage of an underfill adhesive material.
the in-situ measurement of moisture diffusion and hygroscopic expansion of an underfill epoxy material, which is important for the reliability and durability of electronic packages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the underfill material is hygroscopic and the moisture diffusion and hygroscopic strain are significant.
moisture absorption and swelling behavior of the underfill material are highly sensitive to the RH and temperature.
the moisture diffusion and hygroscopic behavior of underfill materials are strongly affected by the temperature and the RH, which should be considered in the design and application of the materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DMA-RH and sorption TGA are two powerful tools to characterize the hygroscopic swelling and moisture absorption behavior of underfill material in-situ, respectively.

the DMA-RH technique is very effective in characterizing the hygroscopic swelling of the underfill material, and the sorption TMA technique provides an accurate measurement of the moisture diffusion coefficient of the underfill materials.
the in-situ characterization techniques developed here can be used to characterize the moisture absorption-desorption, hygroscopic swelling, and hygrothermal aging of underfill materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
moisture diffusion and hygroscopic behavior of an underfull material can be well characterized by in-situ sorption TGA-DMA-RH measurements.
the hygrothermal ageing effect should be taken into account in the design of underfill material.

moisture diffusion and hygroscopic behavior of the underfill material can be well characterized by in-situ techniques, and the results provide useful information to understand the moisture diffusion and hyroscopic behavior of the material.
